feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 9 iunie and again on 7 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 7 mai line is the company of the thirteen Syrian fathers, and doxologia's life of John of Zedazeni names David of Gareji among the twelve disciples. Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 9 iunie — «Sfântul David din Gareji, Georgia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the company, and it is plainly the same company: John out of Syria and the twelve chosen to go into Iberia, whose names the page prints as «Σίω, Δαβίδ, Αντώνιος, Θαδδαίος, Στέφανος, Ισήδωρος, Μιχαήλ, Πύρρος, Ζήνων, Ισέ, Ιωσήφ και Άβιβος». **Thirteen head lines, thirteen names, so thirteen folders**, and the corpus already holds every one of them, so the whole company is upgrades and no folder is created. **`shio-of-mgvime` is the one exception and is not touched**: its `greek` row is already `venerated`, on 4 Φεβρουαρίου, so a reader may not move it; that he is listed here too is a second Greek day and is left in the report. **The Greek adds the whole story of the mission and no years at all**: the flight deeper into the desert when the crowds broke his stillness, the Theotokos appearing in a dream and commanding him to choose twelve and go to Iberia, the names written on separate papers and laid on the holy table, the night of prayer, the twelve papers an angel took from the altar into his hands before them all, the monk Euthymius left as abbot of the skete, the angel warning Bishop Eulogius of the Georgian capital of their coming, the bishop going out with clergy and people to meet them, the wonder like Pentecost by which John spoke Georgian, and their preaching through all Georgia and their veneration of the blessed places Saint Nina had passed, whom the page sends to 14 Ιανουαρίου. **No year, no hymn**, and the page does not say where any of the twelve settled afterwards — the sees and monasteries in their corpus names come from the Romanian side and nothing here is added to them. His head line is «Οσιος Δαβιδ Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη» and the page gives him no epithet, no cave and no Gareji; the folder's Romanian side supplies those and nothing here is added to them.
